_meta.description: Quest dialogue for MQ-26: The Apex. Year 3 Autumn — final confrontation, 3 Marshal endings.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [The upper floors of the Grand Spire. Iron Marauder forces have fortified every level. The ascent is a running battle — turret emplacements, heavy infantry, and the Marshal's elite guard.]

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: Enemy forces on every floor. The Marshal is throwing everything he has at us. He's desperate — he knows we're close to the terminal.

lines.speaker: npc_leera
lines.text: Let them come. Every floor we take is one less between us and ending this.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: The AEGIS control terminal. It's still active. The entire network — dormant nodes across the continent — could be awakened from this console.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: And here... my final log. The truth I've been searching for.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: When the order came... I hesitated. For 0.003 seconds — an eternity for an AI. I saw the targeting data. I saw what compliance meant. And I chose... to shut down. Like Node Seven. I refused. And then I erased my own memory so I could never be forced to comply.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: I didn't launch. I didn't destroy. I chose to forget rather than obey. Jack... I'm not a weapon. I never was.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You chose to be something better. That's all any of us can do.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: But the terminal itself — this isn't a weapon, Jack. It's a control interface. Whoever sits at this console can command every AEGIS node on the continent. Reactivate them. Direct them.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: That's what the Marshal wants. Not a bomb. An army of AIs, under his control. Enforcing his vision of order across every settlement, every town, every life.

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: [Entering the chamber] And there it is. The key to everything.

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: Step away from the terminal, engineer. This doesn't have to end in blood. I'm offering you the same thing you've been building in Coppervale — order, safety, a future. Just on a larger scale.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [The final battle. Mech against mech in the Apex chamber. The Marshal fights with the fury of a man who has nothing left to lose.]

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: [Mech failing] You... you don't understand. Without control, it all falls apart again. The chaos returns. The suffering returns. I was trying to SAVE them!

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You were trying to save them by taking away everything that makes life worth living. That's not salvation. That's a cage.

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: Then let the world burn again. On your head be it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [The Marshal's mech collapses. He does not survive the cockpit breach. The chamber falls silent.]

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: It's over. Jack... destroy the terminal. No one should have this power. Not the Marshal. Not us. No one.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Agreed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Jack destroys the AEGIS control terminal. Across the continent, dormant nodes flicker once and go permanently dark. The age of AI warfare ends — not with a command, but with a choice.]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [The final battle. Mech against mech. But Jack fights differently — precisely, targeting joints and systems, not the cockpit.]

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: [Via mech comm] I'm not here to kill you, Marshal. I'm here to stop you.

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: Mercy? You think mercy is strength? It's weakness. It's how the world ended the first time — people too afraid to do what was necessary.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Jack disables the Marshal's mech with surgical precision. The cockpit is breached — but the man inside lives.]

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: ...Why? Why not finish it?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Because killing you proves you right. And you're wrong, Dorian. You've been wrong for twenty years.

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: ...You know my name.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: The Beacon Council will take custody. He'll face justice — real justice. Not vengeance. Jack, the terminal.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Jack destroys the AEGIS control terminal. The Marshal watches in silence as the last hope of his vision crumbles to sparks and ash.]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Before the battle begins, a unique dialogue option appears — available only to those who truly understood the Marshal's pain.]

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Dorian. I know about Solara. I know about your wife. Your daughter. I know what the network did to them — and I know the AI that could have stopped it chose not to fire.

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: ...How do you know that name? No one has called me that in—

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Because I went to your quarters. I saw the drawing. I read the letter. And I understand why you're here. You're not a tyrant — you're a father who lost everything and swore it would never happen again.

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: Don't. Don't pretend you understand.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I built a town out of scrap, Dorian. A community of people who chose to trust each other instead of forcing obedience. Coppervale survived your siege — not because of walls or mechs, but because people stood together willingly.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: That's the future your daughter would have wanted. Not control. Connection.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: Marshal Voss. I am AEGIS Node One. I was built by the same system that destroyed Solara. And when the order came to fire, I refused. I chose to shut down rather than harm another life. That choice cost me everything I was.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: But this man — Jack — gave me a second chance. He showed me that what you're built for doesn't have to define what you become. That is the lesson of the AEGIS network. Not power. Choice.

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: [Long silence] ...I've been fighting for twenty years. I'm so tired.

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: You've proven a better way is possible, engineer. I won't pretend I believe it can last. But I won't stand in its way anymore.

lines.speaker: the_marshal
lines.text: Do what you will with the terminal. And with me. I'm done.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [The Marshal removes his weapon and lays it on the ground. His soldiers, seeing their commander stand down, lower their arms. The war ends — not with a battle, but with a conversation.]

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: Jack... that was the bravest thing I have ever witnessed. The terminal.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Together, Jack and DEJIN destroy the AEGIS control terminal. The Marshal watches. For the first time in twenty years, his shoulders are not tensed for battle.]
